executiveSummary: The ten Halloween city guides were already published before this period. This week brought a live recheck, a request to close indexing and checkout measurement, and a revised seasonal SEO and answer-engine optimization plan. The prepared plan moves the main production focus toward confirmed November and December events while retaining a smaller Halloween measurement and maintenance track. It is a reviewed proposal, not a claim that the new seasonal optimizations are already published.

work.title: Indexing and measurement follow-up
work.detail: The August report review requested confirmation that the Halloween pages are indexed and tracked, and raised structured data and answer-engine visibility as September priorities. Indexability alone does not establish that Google has indexed a page.
work.whyItMatters: Gives the existing page set a clear measurement follow-up.

work.title: Published Halloween guides rechecked
work.detail: The September 4 public checks found all ten 2026 city guides published, self-canonical and not marked noindex. Remaining checks concern actual indexing, ticket checkout measurement and critical defects.
work.whyItMatters: Preserves completed work and avoids treating ten existing pages as a new build.

work.title: November and December production plan prepared
work.detail: The revised plan prioritizes ten existing URLs: the Ugly Sweater and event hubs, Alpharetta’s November event, the holiday bus pages, and selected December event pages. The inventory review found one November event, twelve Ugly Sweater events and a holiday bus record extending into early January.
work.whyItMatters: Focuses the next sprint on confirmed inventory and existing URLs with distinct search roles.

work.title: Shared template and event markup gaps documented
work.detail: The rendered-page audit found missing H1 headings on the sampled seasonal templates. Existing Event markup needs verified organizer and ticket-offer fields. The plan also calls for resolving competing URLs before creating parallel city guides. These fixes are prepared recommendations.
work.whyItMatters: Targets reusable technical improvements before adding more pages.

decisions.decision: The emailed next step was Halloween measurement followed by older-page optimization. A more specific November and December production plan was prepared afterward and still requires review.

nextSteps.title: Close Halloween measurement
nextSteps.detail: Confirm Google indexing and reconcile checkout starts with completed orders.

nextSteps.title: Approve the seasonal optimization batch
nextSteps.detail: Review the ten existing URLs and the shared H1, internal-link and Event markup changes before implementation.

nextSteps.title: Keep January tied to confirmed inventory
nextSteps.detail: Use the holiday bus’s existing date range; wait for confirmed standalone January events before creating new pages.

caveats: The seasonal plan is an internal review draft; its proposed changes are not presented as deployed.
Search and website data use their own reporting windows. Checkout starts are not completed purchases.
headline: The next season starts here.
